clue.text: Interval a month before a day of triumph

parts.note: Oct is the standard short form of October
VE Day, Victory in Europe Day, marked the Allied triumph in 1945

explanation.surface: Someone counts the days, a month ahead, until a great celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply orders the pieces: the month comes ahead of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the span of eight notes from one C to the next is an interval of that name.

clue.text: A rebuff, say, for a Bohemian

indicators.note: say signals that the word for rebuff is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a check is a sudden stop or setback, a rebuff

explanation.surface: Someone gets a snub and is told it is the sort of thing a free-living artist must expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bohemian' suggests an unconventional artist, but here it means a native of Bohemia, now part of the Czech Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemia is a historic region of the Czech Republic, so a person from there is a native of that country.

clue.text: Make sweet turnover to follow a spring vegetable

indicators.note: to follow places the reversed sweetener after the spring

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: a turnover means the word for make sweet is flipped end to end

parts.note: to sugar something is to make it sweet

explanation.surface: Instructions for sweetening a pastry turnover served after a spring vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like a pastry but turns SUGAR into RAGUS, which follows A SPA. 'spring vegetable' reads as one phrase, but 'spring' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a green garden plant whose young shoots are eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Join up in French material

parts.note: en is the French word for in
list is the selvage or edge strip of woven cloth, a sense of material

explanation.surface: A recruit signs up for a French unit, dressed in its fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To join up is to sign on for military service, as a recruit does.

clue.text: "His sceptre shows the force of ____ power" (Mer of Ven)

definitions.text: "His sceptre shows the force of ____ power" (Mer of Ven)

parts.words: "His sceptre shows the force of ____ power" (Mer of Ven)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Portia's mercy speech in The Merchant of Venice describes the king's sceptre as showing a worldly kind of power, and the missing adjective goes in the grid

explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a blank before 'power'; the answer is the word Shakespeare wrote there in Portia's speech about mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means worldly or secular, as opposed to spiritual, which is the king's kind of authority in the speech.

clue.text: Predestined to take spiritual nourishment, might some say?

definitions.text: Predestined to take spiritual nourishment, might some say?

parts.words: Predestined to take spiritual nourishment, might some say?
parts.note: a pun: someone born fated to receive manna, the heaven-sent food, would be born to the manna, and spoken that way it matches the idiom for being naturally suited to something

explanation.walkthrough: Manna is the food from heaven in Exodus; the phrase spoken with manna sounds the same as the idiom meaning naturally fitted to a role.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone accustomed from birth to a way of life, as if destined for it.

clue.text: The smaller group, being seventeen or less

explanation.surface: A statistic about the smaller faction being made up of teenagers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the lesser part of a group and the legal state of being under eighteen, not yet an adult.

clue.text: Greek character climbing tree first found this fibre

indicators.note: first puts the tree ahead of the Greek letter

parts.note: the oak is a common tree

indicators.note: in a down answer climbing means the letter is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man scales a tree and finds some fibre there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns MU into UM, which follows OAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakum is loose hemp fibre picked from old rope and used to caulk ships' seams.

clue.text: It's a river trip for a self-seeker

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A river cruise is just the thing for an ambitious social climber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey on the river but is the anagram signal for ITSARIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An arriviste is an upstart who pushes ruthlessly for status and personal gain.

clue.text: Citizen lent a piano in need of repair

indicators.note: something in need of repair is broken, so these letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone has loaned out a piano that is badly out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neapolitan is a native or inhabitant of Naples.

clue.text: King appears to vex the church

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
to irk is to annoy or vex

explanation.surface: The monarch seems to be annoying the church authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: KIRK is the Scottish word for a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots word for a church building or the Church of Scotland itself.

clue.text: Quietly he accepts a pay increase, the hypocrite

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: accepts means the word he takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a rise is the British term for a raise in salary

explanation.surface: A man quietly takes a raise in pay, revealing himself as a two-faced fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts A RISE inside HE, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees are portrayed in the Gospels as self-righteous, so the name is used for any sanctimonious pretender.

clue.text: Take away a form

explanation.walkthrough: A form is a British school class; the Remove is a traditional name for one.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove is to take off or away; in some British schools the Remove is a particular class or year group.

clue.text: An old politician to scold, by the sound of him

indicators.note: by the sound of him means the word for scold is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: to wig someone is an old slang term for to scold or rebuke them

explanation.surface: An old-time politician who seems, from how he talks, to be a nag.
explanation.walkthrough: The Whigs were a British party that later became the Liberals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Whigs were a historic British party of the 17th to 19th centuries, so a member is an old-time parliamentarian.

clue.text: See her around before and, in Germany, below this

indicators.note: around means the word her is wrapped round the other letters

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
und is the German word for and

explanation.surface: A reader is told to see a woman's details given earlier and, in the German section, further down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' splits HER as H...ER round EREUND.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means in the part of a document that follows, beneath the present point.

clue.text: Keats is right, perhaps, referring us to a note

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A critic agrees with Keats, citing a footnote as evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges KEATSIS plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: A star-shaped mark in printed text sends the reader to a footnote.

clue.text: Coming round periodically about payment for accommodating wretched dog

indicators.note: accommodating means the joined words for about and payment house the dog inside them

parts.note: re means about or concerning
rent is payment for lodgings
a cur is a mangy, worthless dog

explanation.surface: A landlord grumbles about the rent for housing a miserable mutt, a bill that keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' puts CUR between RE and RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Recurrent things happen again and again at intervals.

clue.text: Burn slowly, soon beginning to turn to dust

indicators.note: beginning means only the opening letter of soon is used

parts.note: to moulder is to decay and crumble away

explanation.surface: Something burning slowly will soon start to crumble into ash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soon beginning' gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: To smoulder is to burn with smoke but no flame.

clue.text: Undergrad new to the island

parts.note: fresh means new
the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea, often just called Man

explanation.surface: A university student who has only just arrived on the island.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshman is a first-year student at college or university.

clue.text: West African seaman, we hear, in this ship's company

indicators.note: we hear means the word for the seaman is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: the Kru, or Kroo, are a Liberian people known as seamen on West African coasts

explanation.surface: A sailor from West Africa is said to be serving on board.
explanation.walkthrough: A Kru, or Kroo, is a member of a Liberian people famous as sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: The crew is the body of people who work a ship.

clue.text: Small gate with a keeper in attendance

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the wicketkeeper is the fielder who stands behind the stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicket is a small door or gate set in a larger one; in cricket the wicket is the set of stumps a wicketkeeper stands behind.

clue.text: Office for ladies' man outside the old city

indicators.note: outside means the word for the ladies' man goes round the city

parts.note: a beau is a dandy or admirer of women
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A womaniser takes an office job beyond the ancient city walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts BEAU round UR.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is an office or department, as in an information bureau.

clue.text: Racecourse records only mares originally established

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records

indicators.note: originally established means only the opening letters of the next words are kept

explanation.surface: A racecourse keeps files showing only mares were bred there from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: EPSOM, in Surrey, is home to the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs in Surrey is a famous English course where the Derby is run.

clue.text: Flyer travelled, it's said, on this American system

indicators.note: it's said means the words for the bird and its journey are taken as spoken

parts.note: a rail is a wading bird, a flyer, and rode means travelled

explanation.surface: A traveller says he flew in on an American transport network.
explanation.walkthrough: A rail is a marsh bird; 'Flyer' looks like an aviator.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US the word is used for a railway network.

clue.text: Tree planted by English student in Lincoln

indicators.note: in means the letters for English student are placed within the name for Lincoln

parts.note: Abe was the familiar name of Abraham Lincoln
L, from learner plates, stands for student

explanation.surface: An English student has planted a tree in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln' reads as the English city but is President Abraham Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: The abele is the white poplar, a kind of tree.

clue.text: Nothing in Latin but rejected poems

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

indicators.note: rejected means the Latin word is turned back

parts.note: sed is the Latin word for but

explanation.surface: No Latin verse here, only rejected poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns SED into DES, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems addressed to a subject.

clue.text: Porter found gold ring after party

indicators.note: after places the gold and ring behind the party

parts.note: do is an informal word for a party
or is the heraldic word for gold
a keeper is a guard ring worn to hold a wedding ring in place

explanation.surface: A hotel porter finds a gold ring left behind after a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A porter in the sense of someone who guards an entrance.

clue.text: Vessel manoeuvring in River Tamar

indicators.note: manoeuvring means these letters are moved about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A boat makes its way along the River Tamar, which divides Devon and Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a sailing boat with three hulls.

clue.text: Bird came first, having a distinguished appellation

parts.note: the tit is a small songbird
led means was in front, came first

explanation.surface: A bird that won the race earns itself a grand name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone titled holds a rank such as lord or lady that forms part of how they are addressed.
